### Combine with `join()`

First, create `tidy_ratings2b`


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tidy_ratings2b <- messy_ratings2b %>%
  select(series, contains("7day")) %>%
  pivot_longer(-series, names_to = "episode", values_to = "viewers") %>%
  separate(episode, into = c("episode", "period")) %>%
  mutate(
    episode = parse_number(episode),
    period = parse_number(period)
  )
```
:::


Why doesn't `left_join()` work? 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tidy_ratings2 %>%
  left_join(tidy_ratings2b)
```

### Combine with `bind_cols`


Why doesn't this work?


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
seasoncols_ratings2 = tidy_ratings2 %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = series, 
              values_from = viewers, 
              names_prefix = "s")

seasoncols_ratings2b = tidy_ratings2b %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = series, values_from = viewers)

seasoncols_ratings2 %>%
  bind_cols(seasoncols_ratings2b)
```

Solve it by removing the episode/period


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
seasoncols_ratings2b = tidy_ratings2b %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = series, 
              values_from = viewers, 
              names_prefix = "s") %>%
  select(-c(episode, period))

seasoncols_ratings2 %>%
  bind_cols(seasoncols_ratings2b)
```

# `join` the episodes data


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tidy_ratings = tidy_ratings2 %>%
  full_join(tidy_ratings2b)
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
episodes = read_csv("https://stat220-s25.github.io/data/bakeoff-episodes.csv")
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
episodes %>%
  left_join(tidy_ratings, by = c("series", "episode")) %>%
  slice_max(viewers, n = 10, with_ties = TRUE) %>%
  select(signature)
```
